key_insight: For linear elastostatics, training finite-element surrogates in the energy norm targets stress accuracy, and minimizing discrete potential energy is exactly equivalent to supervised regression in that norm.
engineering_relevance: Energy-based training supports stress prediction in perforated plates and solids with cavities, where stress concentrations drive engineering decisions.
method: Replace displacement loss with energy-norm supervision.
Train without solution labels by minimizing assembled discrete potential energy.
Screen predictions without solutions: energy ranks candidates for a load case, and its sign flags predictions worse than the zero field.
evidence_signal: In pre-registered comparisons, changing only the supervised loss norm reduced a 3D transformer's median energy-norm error 7.5-fold and median von Mises error 6.1-fold; in 2D, von Mises error more than halved, including on held-out instances.
watch_item: No network transferred to a substantially finer mesh, limiting claims of mesh generalization.
paper_title: The norm, not the labels: training and evaluating finite-element surrogates for stress analysis in the energy norm
